dedupe_keys.name: syncan synthetic can bus intrusion detection dataset

description: SynCAN (Synthetic CAN Bus Data) is a benchmark dataset for evaluating and comparing intrusion detection systems for the controller area network (CAN) bus of vehicles in the signal space. It contains a training set, split into four zip files, and six test sets; every file lists a label (normal or intrusion), one of ten message identifiers, a time stamp in milliseconds and up to four decoded signal values per identifier. The training data contain no intrusions, so detectors are trained unsupervised and tested on normal and attack scenarios. It was released by researchers at ETAS and Bosch as supplementary material to the CANet paper in IEEE Access (2020). Coverage: synthetic signals, not tied to a vehicle model or country. Access: CSV files in the public GitHub repository. Licence and cost: free to download; the repository has no licence file, so reuse terms are unclear beyond the request to cite the paper. Caveats: the signals are synthetic and anonymised, so the physical meaning of each signal is not given, and results may not transfer to real vehicles. It serves cyber-physical resilience studies of road vehicles and connected transport, for example testing how an attack on in-vehicle networks propagates, and complements the CAN-MIRGU real-vehicle attack dataset catalogued in this pass.
